method: Browser-driven crawl (not the check-plan-links.py --audit HTTP-status method -- see note). Executed as same-origin fetch() calls from a real browser session at https://trainingpeaks.com against all 328 rows in training_plans_inventory.csv.
note: check-plan-links.py's HTTP-status approach does not work against TrainingPeaks: confirmed by testing a fabricated plan ID (tp-99999999) and two IDs known dead since July 2026 (443810, 491765) -- all three returned HTTP 200. TrainingPeaks's plan pages are client-rendered; the transport-level response is 200 regardless of whether the plan exists. The reliable signal is page content: a missing plan renders <title>Training Plan Not Found | TrainingPeaks</title>, a real one renders the plan's own name in the title. This crawl checked that signal, not the status code, for every row. check-plan-links.py should be corrected to check title/content, not status, before it's trusted again -- flagged in open-loops.md rather than fixed here (repo-diagnosing-the-repo boundary).
population: All 328 rows in training_plans_inventory.csv (100% of the checkable inventory: has a plan_id and a link). All 328 are currently is_published=TRUE -- there are zero FALSE rows to check in the other direction. That's not a sampling gap: on 2026-08-12 (commit cf07066) all 54 remaining FALSE rows were deleted from the inventory outright rather than resolved one by one, including the '21 genuinely ambiguous' unpublished plans training-plans-analysis.md §11 flagged as still needing this exact link check. They were removed before that check happened, so the FALSE-but-live direction of this audit has had no population to test since August 12.
result: 0 dead links out of 328 published plans. Every plan page rendered its own title, not the 'not found' title. Nothing to flip, nothing to fix.
